title: Discarding cards, at the table and in the shop
summary: Cards leave your hands in two different ways in TCG Card Shop Simulator: the play table has a discard pile that can be searched, and the shop has bins that ask you to confirm before stock is thrown out.
body: Cards leave your possession in two different ways in this game, and the game keeps them apart. There is a discard pile on the play table, which belongs to the card game, and there are bins in the shop, which belong to the business.

The discard pile is a place rather than a counter. It has a starting position, an ending position and a list of positions, so a discarded card travels into the pile instead of simply disappearing from the board.
The pile keeps the cards themselves as objects, including the ones discarded most recently. That is why a card that has been discarded can still be looked at rather than only counted.
The pile has a count element of its own on screen, so how full it is is shown rather than counted by hand.

The pile can be searched. There is a starting position for searching it and a flag that says a search is going on, which means looking through the discard is an action with a state of its own rather than a menu you open.
How many cards are being discarded is a value of its own, and there is a stand-in picture for the discard, so the animation does not have to move the real card every time one leaves the table.
On a controller there is a discard area of its own on the screen, so the action is reachable without a pointer.

In the shop, cards are got rid of by removal rather than by play. The game names kinds of removal, keeps a confirmation screen for the decision and holds a list of bins, so throwing stock away is something you are asked about rather than something that happens quietly.
The picture beside this entry is the game's own: the bin that cards are thrown away in.
What this entry does not tell you: how many cards the pile holds, what searching it costs, or which kind of removal applies to which card. We have not verified those, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: A discarded card travels to a pile with a start position, an end position and a list of positions.
The pile keeps the cards as objects, including the ones discarded most recently.
The pile has a count element on screen.
The pile can be searched, with its own start position and a flag for a search in progress.
How much is discarded is a value of its own, and there is a stand-in picture for the discard.
A controller has a discard area of its own on screen.
Cards are also removed in the shop, with kinds of removal, a confirmation screen and a list of bins.
The game ships its own picture of the bin cards are thrown away in.
Disposing of a card has a sound of its own.
